newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canadian minister criticises EU grain subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Canadian minister criticises EU grain subsidies.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale on Thursday called the European Union's grain export subsidies "counterproductive".
He added that the world grain market could fall into a downward spiral if the United States responded to the subsidies by resorting to its export-enhancement programme.
The sudsidies "could provoke a very unfortunate reaction from the U.S., the export-enhancement programme. Then the world grain market could once again slip into a downward spiral," he said.
Goodale spoke to reporters in Tokyo while on a trade mission with 50 other Canadian business and government officials.

The EU reintroduced its grain export subsidies last year, and senior officials from the U.S.Department of Agriculture criticised the move, hinted that the United States may reintroduce its export-enhancement programme.
Australia has also criticised the subsidies, which the EU is using to help its grain exports.

In mid-1996, when world wheat stocks touched their lowest levels since World War Two, wheat-producing countries did not need to subsidise exports as most stocks were retained for domestic consumption.
But since then, better harvests and rising stocks have given rise to more trade battles over grain.

After the EU reintroduced its export subsidies last year, some U.S. agricultural groups urged the USDA to take retaliatory measures by reinstating its export subsidy programme, the export-enhancement programme.
